title: Caffeine run handover — pairing debrief (Emma Liu)
content:
Notes to self after the 60-minute pairing with candidate (R — referred by Jamal). Had a short caffeine run conversation beforehand (hence the title) — relaxed start, better signal for problem-solving. This is a raw handover for the hiring panel; pull whatever you need and tidy for the committee doc.

High-level impression:
- Strong systems intuition: talked about KV cache eviction tradeoffs clearly, sketched a few heuristics for hot-key detection (LRU-ish variants + TTL sniffing).
- Code fluency: comfortable with Go idioms and concurrent patterns; implemented a small test harness to simulate concurrent batch workers. Some roughness around context cancellation patterns (missed a case where a goroutine leaks if parent cancels immediately).
- Communication: explains rationale rather than reciting facts; asked good clarifying questions when prompt constraints were ambiguous.

Pairing exercise specifics (what we did):
- Task: design & prototype a tiny continuous-batching worker that accepts requests and emits batches to a mock inferencer.
- Candidate implemented: batcher with channel fan-in, timer-based flush, size-based flush, and a simple backpressure signal. Wrote tests for size flush and timer semantics.
- Observed issue: edge-case when batcher is closed during an in-flight timer — their first implementation dropped a few inflight items; they caught it after I nudged about shutdown semantics and iterated.

Signals (positive):
- Ownership: suggested a pragmatic rollout plan (feature flag + canary per region) for changing batch sizes that shows product-aware thinking.
- Pragmatism: prioritizes simple, observable defaults; proposed counters/metrics (batch_size_histogram, flush_latency_p95) that map to our Console dashboards.
- Cross-functional awareness: asked about SLI targets and how this impacts downstream model latencies.

Risks / red flags:
- Distributed systems scale experience is moderate — has mostly single-cluster production experience, limited exposure to multi-region failover.
- Some gaps in advanced Go concurrency patterns (context propagation subtlety). Not fatal but should be checked in follow-up.

Suggested follow-ups for loop:
1) Quick design question for SRE: ask candidate to sketch a multi-region rollback strategy and what metrics trigger automated fallback. Look for understanding of routing policies and graceful degradation.
2) Short homework: fix the shutdown edge-case and add one more property-based test for simultaneous close + timer firing. Patch should be small (<2 hours).
3) Behavioral probe: ask about a time they shipped a change that regressed latency and how they navigated the rollback+communication.

Calibration/leveling notes (for panel):
- Level: L4/L5 boundary — leans L4 given limited multi-region ops, but could be L5 with mentoring and exposure to our infra.
- Likely ramp plan: 30/60/90 focused on (1) production reliability patterns (tracing/metrics), (2) ownership of a small infra feature (batching + rollout), (3) paired ops run with oncall for two weeks.

Actionable items (my recs):
- Proceed to loop with the two follow-ups above; set homework due by EOD two business days after invite.
- Panel anchor: Jamal to lead the systems/concurrency probe, Priya to lead the product/SLI probe.
- If homework is clean and can articulate multi-region rollback plan reasonably, move to onsite or final loop.

Loose thoughts / things to watch in conversation:
- Does candidate mention metrics and how they'll detect functional regressions (not just errors)? Good sign if so.
- Probe deeper on context cancellation pattern — if they can explain the leak and the fix, that elevates confidence quickly.

Random quick notes I scribbled mid-call:
- prefers TTL-heavy eviction for bursty keys
- mentioned "circuit-breaker per model variant" idea (interesting, follow up)
- likes small PRs + observability-first commits

Finish: overall I feel positive but cautious — solid engineer with good instincts, needs a short technical check and a ops/design probe. Will synthesize into the panel doc after collecting Jamal/Priya quick takes.

Emma
(quick: coffee two sugars, prefers async debriefs)
